summary: Lookout south of Aeneas, built 1930 or 1931 (sources differ), used by the Aircraft Warning Service 1942-43, gone by the 1956 USGS visit.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1953; a 1956 USGS visit found the tower and house completely removed.

events.note: Republic News-Miner item says a lookout fireman would be posted there, with horses for emergencies.
Former Fire Lookout Sites register and firelookout.com date the L-4 cab to 1931; Willhite gives 1930; a September 1930 newspaper item describes construction under way.
Panorama photos taken at the site on September 15, 1934.
USGS placed a benchmark there, calling it a high wooded peak with a lookout.
Aircraft Warning Service post, active March 27, 1942 to July 1, 1943; Seattle Filter Center.
USGS visit found the lookout tower and house completely removed; the removal date is not given.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Former Fire Lookout Sites register and firelookout.com give 1931; Willhite gives 1930, and a September 1930 newspaper item describes construction under way. Not resolved by these sources; the story reports both.
Firelookout.com names the Okanogan National Forest; Willhite names the Colville National Forest. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Access is not stated in any source found, so no access field is set (brief says unknown). The brief's elevation (1634.9 m) matches the registry's 1,635 m. The brief's county (Okanogan) is not confirmed by any cached page read. The only staffing evidence is the 1930 newspaper's plan for a lookout fireman and the 1942-43 AWS use; no later staffing. The 1931 vs 1930 build year and the Okanogan vs Colville forest name are unresolved. No source describes the summit today beyond the 1956 USGS finding.
